decisive_items: infectious workup, including inflammatory markers and cultures, was strictly normal
a skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
response.rationale: The vignette shows a non-infectious inflammatory breast process with fistula, peau d'orange, and MRI findings typical of granulomatous lobular mastitis. R5 is the most specific label, combining idiopathic (no infectious cause) and lobular (MRI pattern). R3 is close but lacks lobular specificity.

rejected.why: Periductal mastitis typically involves subareolar ducts; here lesions are diffuse throughout the gland with no ductal predilection.
Granulomatous mastitis is correct but less specific than lobular variant; lacks idiopathic qualifier.
Granulomatous lobular mastitis is correct but omits idiopathic, which is supported by negative infectious workup.
